en.title: The Fed’s Biggest Dove Sees No Clear Path Back to 2% Inflation
en.desc: When even a policymaker known for patience starts sounding alarmed, bond buyers lose a key ally. Goolsbee's warning raises a harder question for anyone holding long Treasuries: what happens if the Fed's last dove stops defending them?

en.title: Bond ETFs Haven’t Been This Rewarding in Years, So Why Is Wall Street Dumping Them?
en.desc: Investors are fleeing bond funds just as new bonds pay the most in years. One yield level will decide whether the exodus was smart or a costly mistake for anyone holding the safe 40% of a portfolio.

en.title: A Monthly Check at 3 Levels of Risk: VTEB, TLT and EMB, Ranked
en.desc: A retiree's monthly bond fund check can stay steady while the share price behind it quietly collapses. Ranking three popular payers on both risks produces two lists that point in opposite directions, and one fund flips from safe to scary.

en.title: Some Fed Officials Wanted to Hike in October. A Half-Point Hike Is on the Table.
en.desc: Fed minutes revealed a hawkish bloc bigger than the October vote let on, and Governor Waller says the central bank may need to shock people. Long bond holders now face a fork where one path rescues them and the other keeps squeezing.

en.title: AGG Lost Money Over 5 Years. Is 60/40 Broken?
en.desc: Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25.

en.title: Treasuries rally for a third day as stocks slip and oil falls
en.desc: Investing.com -- Treasuries rose for a third day as stocks slipped and oil fell. Bloomberg says traders also see much of the Fed’s expected tightening as priced in. All quotes are as of 11:16 AM EST on Nov 18 unless noted.

en.title: Two More Days Above 5% and Treasury Yields Tie 2007’s Run
en.desc: The 10-year yield has spent four straight sessions above a line it rarely crosses, and a bond auction plus Fed minutes arrive within hours. Whether the streak survives could decide what happens next for long-bond holders.

en.title: Traders Now See a 95% Chance the Fed Hikes Rates in December
en.desc: A December hike looks like a lock, yet the Treasury market that matters most for long-bond holders answers to a different signal. Fed officials are split on how far this cycle runs, and TLT owners may be watching the wrong number.

en.title: When SPY Falls 10%, Do Treasury Bonds Still Help?
en.desc: Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036.

en.title: How Much Do You Really Need Invested to Replace a $210,000 Salary With Dividends?
en.desc: The same $210,000 paycheck can cost you $2 million or $6 million in capital, depending on one number. One high-yield holding just slashed its payout, and it shows why chasing the cheapest route can backfire.

en.title: The Government Spends About $5.5 Billion a Day More Than It Takes In. The Debt Has Doubled in 10 Years. Jaime Dimon This the Situation Could Get Much Worse.
en.desc: Washington borrows over a trillion dollars a year just to pay interest on what it already owes, and two of Wall Street's most powerful executives are warning the pressure on bond markets has not yet reached its peak.

en.title: Bessent Tells the Fed Not to Hike “Too Much”
en.desc: Treasury wants the Fed to ease off while the officials who actually vote on rates lean the other way. Long-bond holders sit in the middle of that standoff, and two December dates could decide who wins.

en.title: Kevin Warsh’s Fed Will Vote on Rates Only 7 Times in 2027
en.desc: The Fed is quietly trimming its meeting calendar, and long-term Treasuries already flinched. With a hike looming in December, fewer decision days could make every surprise hit bond holders harder. Which corner of the bond market gets hurt most?

en.title: The U.S. Just Ran Its Biggest October Deficit Ever: $404 Billion
en.desc: A record October gap has a calendar quirk hiding the real story, and bond investors are already reacting. Why do long-dated Treasury funds feel the pain first, and what would prove the bearish case wrong by December?

en.title: How Large Does Your Portfolio Need to Be to Generate $9,400 a Month?
en.desc: Six income holdings, one monthly paycheck target, and a stretch of the portfolio that could vanish in a merger. See which pick carries the shakiest check and which one quietly raises its payout every year.
